## Observations

### Rbit orchestration boundary and librqbit session alternative

`verified` · `@templartorrent.observation.backend-session-comparison/1`

Reviewed rbit 0.2.2 docs (https://docs.rs/rbit/0.2.2/rbit/) and the installed
registry source: rbit supplies protocol primitives, leaving piece selection,
peer coordination, bandwidth and lifecycle to the application. Current local
integration uses those real primitives; it does not assume an upstream Session.

Alternative reviewed: librqbit 9.0.1 has Session::new, add_torrent from magnet,
completion waiting, pause/unpause/delete, session limits and persistence options
in its public documentation (https://docs.rs/librqbit/9.0.1/librqbit/ and
https://docs.rs/librqbit/9.0.1/librqbit/struct.Session.html). Inference: it could
remove substantial generic session/lifecycle infrastructure. No compatibility
proof was established for this project's exact file-rank scheduler, global
payload ownership, private discovery and strict native-source gate. Its desktop
UI is a separate Tauri/web application; that UI is not an option for this contract.
The library can be considered separately from its UI, but replacing rbit conflicts
with AGENTS.md's explicit backend constraint. Retained rbit and did not add a
second backend, external torrent process or another GUI stack.

> **Stale** — `watches "AGENTS.md"` was matched by `cb822df2`, which touched `AGENTS.md`. See [REVIEW-REQUIRED.md](REVIEW-REQUIRED.md#rbit-orchestration-boundary-and-librqbit-session-alternative).

### Linux client writes layout and resume on close and pastes a magnet; remaining boundaries

`verified` · `@templartorrent.observation.complete-piece-status/12`

2026-10-22, Linux x86_64 Ubuntu 26.04.1, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic, rustc 1.99.0, WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0, DISPLAY empty, committed on master at 66c3fea. App::on_exit, the method PixelKit close_slot calls, after one 960 by 640 render at scale 1 wrote that logical size and the inspector split, removed the activation socket, and left a resume bitmap with barrier 1 and bits 1f. The Add dialog's focused magnet field received a system-clipboard magnet on Ctrl+V through the attached clipboard worker, with no clipboard error, and the previous clipboard text was written back. These tests call on_exit and the key callbacks directly. Clippy with denied warnings was clean for the application, all targets. Preview tests, the rest of the workspace suite and the release binary were not re-run. HTTPS tracker announces remain rustls 0.23.46 with aws_lc_rs, certificates checked, ring not compiled. The resume bitmap from f1d59c5 is unchanged. Remaining boundaries: pieces written after the last checkpoint are rechecked and there is no per-block journal; file identity is not a content hash, so an in-place edit that restores inode, size and mtime is not detected; no RTT or reliability scoring, only rates; webseed and UPnP unavailable; download order inside one file follows the seeded tie-break; the rbit fork must be re-applied on any upstream upgrade; Windows paste and a real window event loop are untested.

**supersedes** `@templartorrent.observation.complete-piece-status/11` · **verified_by** `@templartorrent.evidence.announce-transport/1`, `@templartorrent.evidence.https-rustls/1`, `@templartorrent.evidence.https-rustls-audit/1`, `@templartorrent.evidence.multi-lease-before-after/1`, `@templartorrent.evidence.native-audit-after-fork/1`, `@templartorrent.evidence.native-paste/1`, `@templartorrent.evidence.rate-ranking/1`, `@templartorrent.evidence.resume-bitmap/1`, `@templartorrent.evidence.resume-bitmap-gates/1`, `@templartorrent.evidence.window-close/1`, `@templartorrent.evidence.window-close-gates/1`

## Evidence

### Ubuntu 26.04.1, rustc 1.99.0, tree 2b9ca3f plus the rbit fork: 52 adapter tests passed (14 unit, 24 driver, 11 localhost, 3 multiblock). New announce unit tests: the GET keeps a passkey query and percent-encodes binary info hash and peer id, sets Host with a non-default port and Connection: close, and a bare host gets path /; https is refused with "https trackers need TLS support that this client does not build"; HTTP parsing accepts 200 with content length (ignoring trailing bytes) and chunked bodies with extensions, refuses 302, 404, truncated bodies, bad chunk sizes, a missing header terminator and a non-HTTP status line; the body parser reads compact IPv4 and IPv6 peers, dictionary peers, intervals and counts, and refuses failure reasons, missing interval, non-bencode and non-dictionary bodies. The loopback HTTP tracker fixtures in the driver, restore and multiblock tests discovered peers end to end through the new transport.

### Ubuntu 26.04.1, i7-13700H (avx2, sha_ni), rustc 1.99.0, release profile, commit bf22b04, backend detected Avx2, synthetic dense arrays, 500 iterations. eligible p50 ns scalar/auto: 1k pieces 32/36; 100k 939/929 then 697/796 on a repeat run; 1M 7968/6418 with auto p95 20803 versus scalar 9433. reference_piece_pick p50: 1k 3034 ns; 100k 171793 ns then 348377 ns on the repeat with p95 3366847 ns; 1M 4786919 ns with p95 10686525 ns. Finding: the AVX2 eligibility kernel shows no consistent advantage over scalar at any size on this CPU, and the O(P) reference piece pick dominates by two to three orders of magnitude, reaching several milliseconds per pick at 1M pieces. Run-to-run spread at 100k was about 2x on p50, so single runs are not comparable; a laptop on a live desktop session, not an isolated device.
